theory.intro: To find how long a loan takes to repay, set $A_{n}=0$, isolate $(1+r)^{n}$, and solve for $n$ using logarithms. A non-integer result means the loan requires $\lceil n\rceil$ repayments with a smaller final repayment.
facts: Setting $A_{n}=0$ and isolating the growth term gives $(1+r)^{n}=\dfrac{M}{M-PV\,r}$.
If $M\le PV\times r$, repayments do not cover interest and the loan is **never repaid**.
Always round $n$ up to the next integer $\lceil n\rceil$, as a partial period requires an additional repayment.
The smaller final repayment equals $A_{N-1}(1+r)$, where $N=\lceil n\rceil$ and $A_{N-1}$ is the balance before the last payment.
steps: Calculate periodic rate $r$ and verify that $M > PV\times r$.
Take logarithms of both sides to calculate $n=\dfrac{\log\left(\frac{M}{M-PV\,r}\right)}{\log(1+r)}$.
Round up to the integer $\lceil n\rceil$ repayments and compute any partial final repayment.

foundation.question_text: A loan of $\$25\,000$ charges $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.005$). Repayments are $\$600$ per month. Determine the number of monthly repayments needed to pay off the loan.
A company borrows $\$500\,000$ at $5.25\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.004375$) with monthly repayments of $\$10\,000$. Find the number of repayments needed in whole months.
A debt of $\$8000$ incurs interest at $12\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.01$). If repayments are set to $\$70$ per month, explain why the loan will never be repaid.
foundation.solution_text:
$\text{Monthly interest}=8000\times0.01=\$80$
Since the repayment $\$70$ is less than the monthly interest charge $\$80$, the balance increases by $\$10$ each month.
Algebraically, $\dfrac{70}{70-8000(0.01)}=-7\le0$, so the logarithm is undefined and the loan is never repaid.

foundation.question_text: An individual borrows $\$20\,000$ at $7.2\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.006$) with repayments of $\$750$ per month. Find the number of whole repayments required to pay off the loan.
A loan of $\$50\,000$ is taken at $9\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.0075$). What is the exact minimum monthly payment required for the loan to ever reduce?
foundation.solution_text:
$\text{Monthly interest}=50\,000\times0.0075=\$375$
For the loan balance to decrease, the monthly repayment must strictly exceed $\$375$.

foundation.question_text: A loan of $\$12\,000$ at $8\%$ p.a. compounded quarterly ($r=0.02$) is repaid with $\$1000$ per quarter. How many quarters are needed to repay the loan?

development.question_text: A couple has a $\$250\,000$ mortgage at $7.2\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.006$) scheduled for $20$ years ($240$ months). They increase repayments to $\$2000$ per month. Show that $(1.006)^{n}=4$ and find how many months early the loan is paid off.
For a $\$25\,000$ loan at $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.005$) with $\$600$ monthly payments ($n=46.84$ months), calculate the smaller final repayment made on month $47$.

A car loan of $\$30\,000$ at $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.005$) has standard repayments of $\$580$ per month ($60$ months). If the borrower pays $\$700$ per month instead, by how many months is the loan shortened?
For a company loan of $\$500\,000$ at $5.25\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.004375$) with $\$10\,000$ monthly payments ($n=56.55$ months), find the exact final payment on month $57$.
A loan of $\$100\,000$ at $8.4\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.007$) has repayments of $\$700$ per month. Determine whether the loan balance will increase, decrease, or remain constant over time.
development.solution_text:
$\text{Monthly interest}=100\,000\times0.007=\$700$
Since the repayment exactly matches the monthly interest charge ($M=PV\times r$), zero principal is repaid and the balance remains constant at $\$100\,000$.

development.question_text: A loan of $\$15\,000$ is taken at $12\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.01$) with repayments of $\$300$ per month. Find the term of the loan in whole months.

mastery.question_text: A mortgage of $\$400\,000$ at $4.8\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.004$) is repaid with $\$2100$ per month ($360$ months, $30$ years). If payments increase by $\$300$ to $\$2400$ per month, calculate how many years earlier the loan is paid off.

For a loan model $A_{n}=PV(1+r)^{n}-M\left[\dfrac{(1+r)^{n}-1}{r}\right]$, show algebraically that if repayment $M=k\times PV\times r$, the condition for $A_{n}=0$ to have a real positive solution is $k>1$.
mastery.solution_text:
$0=PV(1+r)^{n}-k PV r\left[\dfrac{(1+r)^{n}-1}{r}\right]$
$(1+r)^{n}=k(1+r)^{n}-k\implies(k-1)(1+r)^{n}=k$
$(1+r)^{n}=\dfrac{k}{k-1}$
Since $1+r>1$, $(1+r)^{n}>1$ requires $\dfrac{k}{k-1}>1$.
For $k>1$, $k-1>0$ and $k>k-1$, which holds for all $k>1$.
For $k\le1$, $\dfrac{k}{k-1}\le0$ (or undefined), so no real solution exists.

mastery.question_text: A personal loan of $\$10\,000$ at $12\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.01$) is repaid with $\$450$ per month. Find the total number of repayments $N$ and the exact final payment $M_{\text{final}}$ on month $N$.
